title: Enforce finite spatial inputs and the influence cap in LinearBlendSkinning
description:
## Summary

Make the geometry-binding/skinning contract reject the invalid spatial inputs it currently trusts, and make the advertised influence-count cap an enforced invariant. Two independent external audits converged on this at the same code site.

Provenance: `docs/audits/creaturecreator-deep-dive-code-review-audit-26-09-05-23-07-45.md` F2 (P1/P2) and F3 (P2); `docs/audits/creaturecreator-deep-dive-code-review-2026-09-05.md` P1 (influence count) and P1 (binding finite inputs). Verified at current HEAD `99fe6ad`; no existing TSK owns this bounded scope (broad owner family: TSK-0077 / CC-073).

## Scope

`Assets/Scripts/Runtime/Animation/Binding/LinearBlendSkinning.cs` (`Deform`, `BonePose`):

- Reject non-finite values in `restVertices` and in every `rest`/`posed` bone frame (`BonePose.Position`, `BonePose.Rotation`) using the existing shared guard `ProceduralCreature.Common.NumericValidity.IsFinite(Vector3)` / `IsFinite(Quaternion)`. Do not add a new finite utility; one already exists.
- Make the `MaxBoneInfluencesPerVertex = 4` contract an executable invariant. Choose and record one contract: reject `influences.Count > MaxBoneInfluencesPerVertex` inside `Deform`, or enforce the cap at the binding authoring/build stage and document that `Deform` accepts the already-validated representation. Keep the chosen contract explicit in the XML docs.
- Decide and state whether a bone rotation must be only finite, or finite and normalized/non-degenerate; document that invariant on `BonePose`.
- Do not change weighting math, rest-pose round-trip behavior, or the welded-Body out-of-scope note.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `Deform` throws `DomainException` on a NaN/Infinity in a rest vertex, a rest `BonePose.Position`, a rest `BonePose.Rotation`, a posed `BonePose.Position`, or a posed `BonePose.Rotation` (one focused test per field).
- `Deform` throws `DomainException` for a vertex with five otherwise-valid influences when the hard-invariant contract is chosen (or, if the authoring-stage contract is chosen, the authoring/validation path rejects >4 and a test proves it).
- A valid finite binding still passes and reproduces the existing rest-pose round-trip result.
- No behavior change outside the corrected non-finite and over-cap cases.

## Validation

Focused runtime tests under `Assets/Scripts/Tests/Runtime/` (the existing skinning test fixture) covering each non-finite field and the >4-influence case. Then run the full runtime EditMode/PlayMode suites in Unity. Static source inspection alone cannot close this task.

## Findings

- `Deform` validates null/count/weight/bone-index but never validates `restVertices`, `rest[].Position/Rotation`, or `posed[].Position/Rotation`; a single NaN propagates through `Quaternion.Inverse` and blending into a non-finite mesh position.
- `MaxBoneInfluencesPerVertex` appears only in the declaration/docs and TSK-0077 evidence; no production check or test references the constant.
- The module already uses a strict finite-weight contract, so accepting non-finite geometry is inconsistent with its own defensive contract.

## Blockers

None known. Shared `NumericValidity.IsFinite` already exists.

## Next Step

Implement the finite guards and the influence-cap decision, then add the focused tests above.

comments.body:
## Sprint Round 1 evidence (2026-09-05/06, deep-dive hardening sprint, fixed point 5f7205f)

Implemented finite spatial-input validation and influence-cap enforcement in LinearBlendSkinning.

Changed files:
- Assets/Scripts/Runtime/Animation/Binding/LinearBlendSkinning.cs — added ValidateBoneFrame finite checks (rest and posed Position/Rotation) applied to the whole arrays in the single pre-loop that builds inverseRestRotation (no extra O(bones) pass); per-vertex finite rest-vertex check and influences.Count > MaxBoneInfluencesPerVertex rejection before bind math; documented the FINITE CONTRACT (F2/F3) and WEIGHT CONVENTION on the class and BonePose.
- Assets/Scripts/Tests/Runtime/LinearBlendSkinningTests.cs — 6 focused tests: Deform_TooManyInfluences_Throws, Deform_NonFiniteRestVertex_Throws (NaN+Inf), Deform_NonFiniteRestPosition_Throws, Deform_NonFiniteRestRotation_Throws, Deform_NonFinitePosedPosition_Throws, Deform_NonFinitePosedRotation_Throws (all Assert.Throws<DomainException>).

Decisions (flagged, non-obvious):
1. Influence-cap contract = reject inside Deform, not at an authoring/build stage: no production binding-authoring stage exists (all VertexInfluence construction is test-only), so Deform is the single enforcement boundary and already validates per-vertex there. Documented on the const and WEIGHT CONVENTION.
2. Rotations enforced finite-only, NOT normalized: bounded scope forbids changing normalization behavior; documented on BonePose that rotations are expected to be proper unit rotations kept normalized by the caller.
3. Shared guard reused: NumericValidity.IsFinite(Vector3/Quaternion); no new finite utility, no competing binding path.

Validation:
- dotnet build ProceduralCreature.Runtime.csproj --no-restore: 0 errors/0 warnings.
- dotnet build ProceduralCreature.Tests.Runtime.csproj --no-restore: 0 errors/0 warnings.
- git diff --check: clean.
- Unity connected (port 6401): refresh compile 0 console errors; PlayMode runtime assembly ProceduralCreature.Tests.Runtime passed 501/501 (run twice, consistent), including the new cases. (Note: EditMode does not discover the runtime assembly in this project; narrow PlayMode test_names filters timed out at MCP init, so validated via full-assembly PlayMode run.)

Residual risk: finite-only enforcement means a zero/degenerate (finite, length-0) quaternion would still make Quaternion.Inverse return NaN downstream; rotations expected to be kept proper/normalized by callers. This is documented and consistent with the out-of-scope "do not change normalization" constraint. No commit/push made by subagent.
